hypothesis: If the generated ERA5 pressure-level Zarr pipeline preserves lossless Blosc-Zstd clevel=9 bitshuffle and one-time, one-pressure-level, full-latitude/full-longitude chunks, but groups requested channels that share the same native variable into one data array with a real selected pressure-level coordinate/dimension for that native-variable group, then output_bytes may decrease through fewer data arrays and less duplicated metadata while consumer_samples_per_second may improve slightly by reducing array traversal/metadata overhead. Every channel must still be declared separately with its field_id, selector value, array_path, and selector coordinate path, and no unrequested data planes may be materialized.
reflection: The parent p010 is feasible and strong on footprint with Zarr v3, full-spatial sample/selector chunks, and Blosc-Zstd clevel=9 bitshuffle, but it publishes one data array per requested field-selector channel. Prior feasible grouped same-native-variable compressed runs (notably p014 and p018) preserved the same codec and chunk topology while grouping temperature 500/850 into one native variable array with a real selector dimension, yielding slightly lower output bytes and slightly higher measured throughput than p010. The current slot is joint, so the most bounded mutation is not changing compression strength or chunk spatial topology, but changing only data-array organization to group requested pressure levels that share a native variable. This targets both scheduled objectives while preserving exact values, selected fields, selector coordinates, dimensions, and artifact channel declarations.
